external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: Customer who browses and places orders through the mobile app and receives a faxed confirmation.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: Mobile application used by customers to browse and order socks.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: API used by the mobile app; it stores customer information, accepts orders, and sends orders to SIMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: Stock and inventory system that receives orders, writes delivery addresses to a flat file, and sends dispatch notes to the fax gateway.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: Gateway that sends dispatch confirmations by fax to the customer using the number stored against the order.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway
processes.notes: Nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

processes.name: macros
processes.description: Macros in the marketing spreadsheet that send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API
processes.notes: It was a stopgap and it is still here.

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: Database containing customer names, addresses, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database ... [is] encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: Flat file kept alongside SIMS containing delivery addresses only.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the ... flat file [is] encrypted.

data_stores.name: spreadsheet
data_stores.description: Marketing spreadsheet containing the product catalogue; its macros change prices and product copy through the web API.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet
data_stores.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.description: Customer browses and places orders through the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: send requests
data_flows.description: The mobile app communicates with the web API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP

data_flows.name: keep customers
data_flows.description: The web API keeps customer names, addresses, and payment card information in the user database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
data_flows.data_description: customer name, address, and the card they paid with

data_flows.name: hand order
data_flows.description: The web API hands an order over to SIMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write address
data_flows.description: SIMS writes the delivery address into the flat file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.description: SIMS sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.description: The fax gateway faxes the customer a confirmation containing their name and address.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

data_flows.name: change prices
data_flows.description: Spreadsheet macros send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy
